shlokas.sanskrit: कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य रामे धर्मपरे स्थिते । कालस्तापसरूपेण राजद्वारमुपागमत् ।। 7.103.1 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: kasyacittvatha kālasya rāme dharmapare sthite | kālastāpasarūpeṇa rājadvāramupāgamat || 7.103.1 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Now, after some time had passed, while Rama remained devoted to righteousness, Time, in the form of an ascetic, came to the gate of the palace.

shlokas.sanskrit: सो ऽब्रवील्लक्ष्मणं वाक्यं धृतिमन्तं यशश्विनम् । मां निवेदय रामाय सम्प्राप्तं कार्यगौरवात् ।। 7.103.2 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: so 'bravīllakṣmaṇaṃ vākyaṃ dhṛtimantaṃ yaśaśvinam | māṃ nivedaya rāmāya samprāptaṃ kāryagauravāt || 7.103.2 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: He spoke this word to Lakshmana, the steadfast and illustrious one: "Announce me to Rama, for I have come on a matter of grave importance."

shlokas.sanskrit: दूतो ऽस्म्यतिबलस्याहं महर्षेरमितौजसः । रामं दिदृक्षुरायातः कार्येण हि महाबल ।। 7.103.3 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: dūto 'smyatibalasyāhaṃ maharṣeramitaujasaḥ | rāmaṃ didṛkṣurāyātaḥ kāryeṇa hi mahābala || 7.103.3 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "I am the messenger of a great sage of immense strength and immeasurable energy. O mighty one, I have come, desiring to see Rama upon an errand."

shlokas.sanskrit: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सौमित्रिस्त्वरया ऽन्वितः । न्यवेदयत रामाय तापसं तं समागतम् ।। 7.103.4 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā saumitristvarayā 'nvitaḥ | nyavedayata rāmāya tāpasaṃ taṃ samāgatam || 7.103.4 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Hearing those words of his, the son of Sumitra, filled with haste, announced to Rama that the ascetic had arrived.

shlokas.sanskrit: जयस्व राम धर्मेण उभौ लोकौ महाद्युते । दूतस्त्वां द्रष्टुमायातस्तपसा भास्करप्रभः ।। 7.103.5 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: jayasva rāma dharmeṇa ubhau lokau mahādyute | dūtastvāṃ draṣṭumāyātastapasā bhāskaraprabhaḥ || 7.103.5 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "Be victorious in both worlds through righteousness, O Rama of great splendor! A messenger, radiant as the sun through his austerity, has come to see you."

shlokas.sanskrit: तद्वाक्यं लक्ष्मणेनोक्तं श्रुत्वा राम उवाच ह । प्रवेश्यतां मुनिस्तात महौजास्तस्य वाक्यधृत् ।। 7.103.6 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tadvākyaṃ lakṣmaṇenoktaṃ śrutvā rāma uvāca ha | praveśyatāṃ munistāta mahaujāstasya vākyadhṛt || 7.103.6 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Hearing those words spoken by Lakshmana, Rama said: "Let the sage be ushered in, dear one — that one of great energy, the bearer of his master's message."

shlokas.sanskrit: सौमित्रिस्तु तथेत्युक्त्वा प्रावेशयत तं मुनिम् । ज्वलन्तमेव तेजोभिः प्रदहन्तमिवांशुभिः ।। 7.103.7 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: saumitristu tathetyuktvā prāveśayata taṃ munim | jvalantameva tejobhiḥ pradahantamivāṃśubhiḥ || 7.103.7 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Saumitri, saying "So be it," ushered in that sage, who was blazing with his splendor and seemed to scorch all around him with his rays.

shlokas.sanskrit: सो ऽभिगम्य रघुश्रेष्ठं दीप्यपानं स्वतेजसा । ऋषिर्मधुरया वाचा वर्धस्वेत्याह राघवम् ।। 7.103.8 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: so 'bhigamya raghuśreṣṭhaṃ dīpyapānaṃ svatejasā | ṛṣirmadhurayā vācā vardhasvetyāha rāghavam || 7.103.8 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Approaching that best of the Raghus, who shone with his own radiance, the sage in sweet words said to Raghava, "May you prosper!"

shlokas.sanskrit: तस्मै रामो महातेजाः पूजामर्घ्यपुरोगमाम् । ददौ कुशलमव्यग्रं प्रष्टुमेवोपचक्रमे ।। 7.103.9 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tasmai rāmo mahātejāḥ pūjāmarghyapurogamām | dadau kuśalamavyagraṃ praṣṭumevopacakrame || 7.103.9 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Rama of great splendor gave him honor beginning with the arghya offering, and then, calm and composed, proceeded to inquire after his welfare.

shlokas.sanskrit: पृष्टश्च कुशलं तेन रामेण वदतां वरः । आसने काञ्चने दिव्ये निषसाद महायशाः ।। 7.103.10 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: pṛṣṭaśca kuśalaṃ tena rāmeṇa vadatāṃ varaḥ | āsane kāñcane divye niṣasāda mahāyaśāḥ || 7.103.10 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Being asked after his welfare by Rama, that best of speakers, the renowned sage, sat down upon a divine golden seat.

shlokas.sanskrit: तमुवाच ततो रामः स्वागतं ते महामुने । प्रापयास्य च वाक्यानि यतो दूतस्त्वमागतः ।। 7.103.11 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tamuvāca tato rāmaḥ svāgataṃ te mahāmune | prāpayāsya ca vākyāni yato dūtastvamāgataḥ || 7.103.11 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then Rama said to him, "Welcome to you, great sage. Deliver the words of him from whom you have come as a messenger."

shlokas.sanskrit: चोदितो राजसिंहेन मुनिर्वाक्यमभाषत । द्वन्द्वमेतत्प्रवक्तव्यं हितं वै यद्यपेक्षसे ।। 7.103.12 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: codito rājasiṃhena munirvākyamabhāṣata | dvandvametatpravaktavyaṃ hitaṃ vai yadyapekṣase || 7.103.12 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Urged on by the lion among kings, the sage spoke these words: "This is to be told between the two of us alone, if indeed you desire what is beneficial."

shlokas.sanskrit: यः शृणोति निरीक्षेद्वा स वध्यो भविता तव । भवेद्वै मुनिमुख्यस्य वचनं यद्यपेक्षसे ।। 7.103.13 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: yaḥ śṛṇoti nirīkṣedvā sa vadhyo bhavitā tava | bhavedvai munimukhyasya vacanaṃ yadyapekṣase || 7.103.13 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "Whoever hears or looks upon it shall become one to be slain by you — so it must be, if you heed the word of the foremost of sages."

shlokas.sanskrit: स तथेति प्रतिज्ञाय रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत् । द्वारि तिष्ठ महाबाहो प्रतिहारं विसर्जय ।। 7.103.14 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: sa tatheti pratijñāya rāmo lakṣmaṇamabravīt | dvāri tiṣṭha mahābāho pratihāraṃ visarjaya || 7.103.14 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Promising "So be it," Rama said to Lakshmana, "Stand at the door, O mighty-armed one, and dismiss the doorkeeper."

shlokas.sanskrit: स मे वध्यः खलु भवेत् कथाद्वन्द्वं समीरितम् । ऋषेर्मम च सौमित्रे पश्येद्वा शृणुयाच्च यः ।। 7.103.15 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: sa me vadhyaḥ khalu bhavet kathādvandvaṃ samīritam | ṛṣermama ca saumitre paśyedvā śṛṇuyācca yaḥ || 7.103.15 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "O Saumitri, whoever should see or hear this private conversation now spoken between the sage and myself must surely be put to death by me."

shlokas.sanskrit: ततो निक्षिप्य काकुत्स्थो लक्ष्मणं द्वारि सङ्ग्रहम् । तमुवाच मुने वाक्यं कथयस्वेति राघवः ।। 7.103.16 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tato nikṣipya kākutstho lakṣmaṇaṃ dvāri saṅgraham | tamuvāca mune vākyaṃ kathayasveti rāghavaḥ || 7.103.16 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then Kakutstha, having stationed Lakshmana at the door as guard, Raghava said to him, "Sage, speak your words."

shlokas.sanskrit: यत्ते मनीषितं वाक्यं येन वा ऽसि समाहितः । कथयस्वाविशङ्कस्त्वं ममापि हृदि वर्तते ।। 7.103.17 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: yatte manīṣitaṃ vākyaṃ yena vā 'si samāhitaḥ | kathayasvāviśaṅkastvaṃ mamāpi hṛdi vartate || 7.103.17 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "Whatever message you have resolved upon, or by whatever charge you have been entrusted, speak it without hesitation — it rests in my heart as well."

shlokas.sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे त्र्युत्तरशततमः सर्गः ।। 103 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmaduttarakāṇḍe tryuttaraśatatamaḥ sargaḥ || 103 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Thus in the sacred Ramayana, the first poem composed by Valmiki, in the venerable Uttara Kanda, ends the one hundred and third sarga.
